source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:25 ('אל מקומי — an old Torah-scroll manual records מקמי lean in one book, but the Ramah wrote that it is FULL with vav')
claim_en: MY-PLACE WRITTEN FULL: מקומי ('to MY PLACE,' 30:25 — the first word of Jacob's send-me demand) carries its vav as the Ramah rules, against the one old book's recorded lean form: the place-word of the never-performed send written whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:27 ('ויברכני — the resh with SHEVA')
claim_en: THE BLESS-WORD'S HALF-VOWEL, STATION ELEVEN: ויברכני ('and YHWH has BLESSED ME' — in Laban's mouth, by divination) — Minchat Shai rules the resh with plain sheva (the silent half-vowel); SNAPSHOT points hataf patach (the compound half-vowel), the characterized class's eleventh station and the bless-word family's fifth — the ruled-vs-pointed split holding its exact shape on a resh once more.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:30 ('גם אנכי — the gimel SOFT')
claim_en: THE SOFT GIMEL OF ALSO-I: גם ('when shall I provide for my house, ALSO I,' 30:30) — the gimel soft, no doubling dot, exactly as ruled: the whole token in the stream is gimel-patach-mem, nothing between.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:31 ('תתן לי — the lamed SOFT')
claim_en: THE SOFT LAMED OF GIVE-ME-NOTHING: לי ('you shall not give ME anything,' 30:31 — Jacob refusing a paid wage) — the lamed soft as ruled, the hiriq (the i-vowel) sitting directly on the undoubled letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:32 ('שה חום — with MAQQEF and not with meteg on the shin; so in the books and in Ben Asher's handwritten variant-lists')
claim_en: THE LAMB JOINED, NOT STRESSED: שה ('every DARK LAMB among the sheep,' 30:32 — the wage being named) — joined to its color-word by maqqef (the joining stroke) with NO meteg (the small stress-stroke) on the shin, exactly as Minchat Shai rules from the books and Ben Asher's own variant-lists: the whole token is shin-segol-he, bare of any stroke.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:33 ('איננו נקד — Hilleli lean, Yerushalmi full; in ALL the books lean like the first one in the previous verse, and the Masorah marks the pair 2-lean; the Ramah: every speckled-word in the Torah is written lean, no vav')
claim_en: THE SPECKLED-WORD LEAN, AND LEAN EVERYWHERE: נקד ('SPECKLED') stands bare exactly twice — the wage named (30:32) and the wage audited ('whatever is not speckled... is stolen,' 30:33) — both lean with the Hilleli and all the books against the Yerushalmi's full form, and the Ramah's whole-Torah rule holds: no full-spelled speckled-form exists anywhere in the Torah (builder-checked across every prefixed and suffixed form).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:35 ('העזים — the zayin DAGESHED')
claim_en: THE SHE-GOATS' DOUBLING DOT: העזים ('the SHE-GOATS,' 30:35 — Laban removing the speckled stock that same day) — the zayin dageshed (the doubling dot) exactly as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:36 ('הנותרת — Bereshit Rabbah 73: Resh Lakish says it is WRITTEN נתרת [dropped-out]; but the Masorah here and in Jeremiah counts הנותרת 3 — two lean and one full, the signs: the flock of Laban, according-to-the-years (Bechukotai), and the-army-of-the-king-of-Babylon (Jer 34:7), the last one full; and so the Ramah')
claim_en: THE REMAINING FLOCK AND THE SKELETON COLLISION: the letter-skeleton הנותרת stands exactly three times in the Torah — but only two are the Masorah's word: the plural 'the flock REMAINING' (30:36) and 'according to the years REMAINING' (Lev 27:18), both written lean without the second vav exactly as the Masorah and the Ramah rule (Jeremiah's full third stands outside, named); the third Torah token (Lev 10:12) is the SINGULAR 'the meal-offering that remains,' a different word — and it is precisely the plural's missing vav that collapses the two words into one skeleton. SNAPSHOT stands with the Masorah's written form against Resh Lakish's doubly-dropped נתרת.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:36 (the Masorah's lean ruling on this token)
claim_en: AND THE LEAN LETTERS THEMSELVES: at 30:36 the remaining-word ends resh-holam-tav — the o-vowel carried by the point alone, no vav in the letters, the Masorah's lean ruling sitting in the stream codepoint by codepoint.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:37 ('לבנה — the nun with SEGOL')
claim_en: THE POPLAR'S SEGOL: לבנה ('a rod of fresh POPLAR,' 30:37 — the first of the three rod-trees) — the nun in segol (the short e) exactly as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:38 ('פצל — in ALL the books the tzadi in TZERE; the Mikraot Gedolot printer wrote that the tzadi takes segol and all the pointers err — but HE is the one erring: the rule is tzere, as the Michlol and Livyat Chen state')
claim_en: THE PEEL-VERB'S LONG E: פצל ('the rods that he had PEELED,' 30:38) — the tzadi dageshed and in tzere (the long e) with all the books, the Michlol, and Minchat Shai's own arbitration, against the printer who called every pointer mistaken: the printed segol refuted in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:38 ('בשקתות — in OUR books the qof with sheva-and-patach [the compound half-vowel]; but the Michlol (p. 187) counted it among those written with sheva ALONE, read as compound because of the meteg that comes with the hiriq')
claim_en: THE TROUGHS' SPLIT HALF-VOWEL — THE CLASS TAKES A QOF: בשקתות ('in the water TROUGHS,' 30:38) — the tradition itself divides: Minchat Shai's books write the qof with hataf patach (the compound half-vowel), the Michlol's precise books with plain sheva, compound only in the mouth by force of the meteg on the hiriq before it. SNAPSHOT joins Minchat Shai's camp — written hataf — while carrying the Michlol's driving meteg in the same word: the fourth split-attested station, and the class's first QOF, a fourth consonant for the consonant-general law.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:38 ('ויחמנה — the Masorah: THREE words are androgynous, carrying the signs of male and female both — ויחמנה here, וישרנה of the cows (I Sam 6:12), יעמדנה of the four kingdoms (Dan 8:22): yod at their head, nun-he at their tail, the male preceding the female')
claim_en: THE ANDROGYNOUS VERB AT THE TROUGHS: ויחמנה ('and they CAME INTO HEAT when they came to drink,' 30:38) — the Masorah's three-word list of forms bearing both signs: the masculine yod at the head, the feminine nun-he at the tail, 'the male preceding the female.' The Torah's one member carries exactly that skeleton in the stream (yod first, nun-he last); the cows of Beth Shemesh and Daniel's four kingdoms stand outside, named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:40 ('ולא שתם על צאן לבן — an old chumash records it among the sevirin: the sense EXPECTS עם [with], the letter WRITES על [on], with ועשית-חסד (I Sam 20:8) and זכרה-לי (Nehemiah) as companions')
claim_en: THE SEVIRIN 'ON': ולא שתם על צאן לבן ('he did not set them ON the flock of Laban,' 30:40) — the sense expects WITH (עם); the letter writes ON (על), and the written form stands in the stream: the sevirin class (expected-but-not-written readings the Masorah itself lists) takes its second in-corpus member after Sodom's morning (19:23), the companions in Samuel and Nehemiah named outside.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:41 ('המקשרות — the mem SOFT; in a minority of books the mem carries a meteg')
claim_en: THE BOUND-UP FLOCK'S SOFT MEM: המקשרות ('the STURDY [bound-up] ones of the flock,' 30:41 — the ones Jacob set the rods before) — the mem soft with plain sheva, no doubling dot and no meteg, joining Minchat Shai's primary ruling against the minority books' meteg camp.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:41 ('ליחמנה — the mem in TZERE in the precise Sephardic books and the early print; so the Michlol (p. 42), found so in the exact books')
claim_en: THE HEAT-VERB'S LONG E: ליחמנה ('that they might COME INTO HEAT at the rods,' 30:41) — the mem in tzere (the long e) with the precise Sephardic books, the early print, and the Michlol's exact-book collation.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 30:42 ('העטופים — 2 in the Masorah: the FEEBLE ones to Laban, and the ones WRAPPED in famine (Lam 2:19): he gave Laban the feeble that die in famine — or: because Jacob did a thing that looked like trickery, his sons were wrapped in famine')
claim_en: THE FEEBLE ONES AND THE FAMINE: העטפים ('the FEEBLE ones were Laban's,' 30:42) — the word's only Torah token, paired by the Masorah with 'the ones WRAPPED in famine at the head of every street' (Lam 2:19, named): the feeble stock left to Laban answered by children wrapped in famine, measure spoken for measure. And the letters carry a quiet variance: the Kitzur's headword cites the pair full with vav; SNAPSHOT writes the Torah member LEAN, the u-vowel carried by the point alone.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 30:33 ('ביום מחר — 2 in the Masorah: here, and Do-not-boast about TOMORROW'S DAY (Prov 27:1). The Holy One said to Jacob: do you know what tomorrow brings? Do not boast of tomorrow — tomorrow your daughter Dinah goes out from you')
claim_en: TOMORROW'S DAY, SPOKEN ONCE: ביום מחר ('so shall my righteousness answer for me IN THE DAY TO COME,' 30:33) — the two-word form stands exactly once in the Torah, at Jacob's one boast about tomorrow; the Masorah's partner is the proverb 'do not boast about the day to come' (Prov 27:1, named) — and the Kitzur hears the rebuke arm itself here, at the gate of the Dinah chapters.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:42 ('ובהעטיף — in the handwritten variant-lists, the vav and the tet alone carry meteg according to Ben Asher, and so in the precise books')
claim_en: THE WRAPPING-VERB'S ABSENT STROKES: ובהעטיף ('and when the flock was FEEBLE he would not set them,' 30:42) — Ben Asher's precise books carry meteg (the small stress-stroke) on the vav and the tet; SNAPSHOT's token carries neither, only the merkha cantillation on the tet: the meteg-omission class takes its fourth member (after 28:6, gen_47's sub-variance, and 30:16).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:42 ('ובהעטיף — some printed books make the pe RABBATI [large], and so one of the two large-letter alphabets and the Masorah at the head of Bereshit and the scroll-manual; but many precise manuscripts and early prints do NOT, and the Masorah at the head of Chronicles does not count it among the large letters')
claim_en: THE LARGE-PE QUESTION (letter-size layer, uninstrumented): the pe of ובהעטיף — the tradition itself divides on whether it is written large, and Minchat Shai sides with the precise books AGAINST the enlargement; SNAPSHOT's stream carries no letter-size layer, so the question is filed, not settled: the letter-size gap's in-span member.
